fields.h1: Build a Donation Receipt Form That Writes the Receipt for You
fields.hero_description: Build a donation receipt form that turns each logged gift into a numbered receipt, saved in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Every Receipt, Filled From the Gift Record
fields.features_subheading: A paper receipt book leaves staff copying names and amounts by hand. Here, the app fills each receipt from the gift staff just logged.
fields.feature_1:
Describe the receipt, get the form behind it

Describe the receipt your office sends and the gifts it covers. Emergent builds the entry form, the receipt layout, and the donor tables, then changes them when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Fields that change with the kind of gift

Pick cash or check and the form asks for the amount and the date received. Pick donated goods and it asks for a description of each item instead, with no box for a dollar value.
fields.feature_3:
Receipt numbers that count up by one

Each saved gift takes the next number in the year's series, such as 2026-0418. The treasurer can match any receipt to its gift record and see at a glance if a number is missing.
fields.feature_4:
Online gifts receipted with no typing

Connect the Stripe account your online gifts run through. Each completed payment fills a receipt record with the donor, amount, and date, like a gift logged at the front desk.
fields.feature_5:
A heads-up when a receipt needs a person

Gifts of goods and gala tickets post a Slack message to your development channel saying a receipt is waiting, with a link to the record. Names and amounts stay in the database.
fields.feature_6:
Your receipt app, in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and host the receipt app beside your donor system. The receipt layout and the numbering rules move with the code.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Gifts, Four Kinds of Receipt
fields.tab_content_1:
By noon, Imelda's $400 check has its receipt

Imelda Strathcove's $400 check to Tamarack Valley Food Bank becomes receipt 2026-0418. The IRS says the written acknowledgment for a gift of $250 or more must contain the organization's name and the cash amount. Her emailed receipt has both, plus a line stating that no goods or services were provided.
fields.tab_content_2:
From the loading dock, a receipt with no dollar value

Gareth Ovington drops off a sofa and 2 bookcases at Old Mill Reuse Center's dock, and the dock lead logs them on a tablet. The IRS lists a description, but not the value, of a non-cash contribution among the contents of a written acknowledgment. His receipt describes each piece and its condition, with no dollar figure.
fields.tab_content_3:
When a $150 gala seat includes a $60 dinner

Quillmarsh Youth Orchestra sells gala seats at $150, each with a dinner it values at $60. The IRS requires a disclosure statement when a donor's quid pro quo payment is more than $75, giving a good faith estimate of what the donor received. Every gala receipt states the $60 estimate beside the price paid.
fields.tab_content_4:
In January, one statement for 12 gifts of $30

Rosamund Vesterholm gives Kestwood Animal Shelter $30 a month by card. In early January, the app gathers her 12 gifts from the year before into one statement, each with its date and amount, $360 in all. She gets it by email, and the shelter's copy stays on her donor record for the day she asks for it again.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Donation Receipt Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a donation receipt form that gives each kind of gift the right receipt, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List every way gifts reach you
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask each gift type only what it needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the ways gifts arrive today: checks at the front desk, card payments online, furniture at the dock, gala tickets. Each one becomes a gift type on the form, with its own questions and its own receipt layout.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Enter the legal name your receipts carry and the address donors know. Then write the line a receipt uses when the donor got nothing back, in the words your board or your accountant has approved.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A check needs its amount and the day it came in. Donated goods need a description of each item and its condition. Gala tickets need the price paid and your estimate of what the guest received.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Start the series at the number your paper receipt book would have used next, so the records run on without a break. Put the year in front, and the count starts again at 0001 each January.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect the payment account your website gifts go through, so each completed payment creates a gift record. Run one small gift through it first and check that the name, amount, and date match the payment.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick the receipts a staff member reads before they go out, such as goods a volunteer described at the dock. Those wait in a review list. Every other receipt is sent as soon as the gift is saved.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test with one gift of each type
fields.howto_step_7_des: Log a test gift for each type and read every receipt the way a donor would. Check the number series, the goods descriptions, and the gala estimate, then delete the test records before the first real gift.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a donation receipt form for my food bank that emails each donor a numbered receipt once staff log the gift.

faq_plan.q: What is a donation receipt form?
How do I create a donation receipt form?

plan.angle: The top 10 for donation receipt form are printable PDF and Word templates (eForms, Invoice Simple, a Goodwill PDF) and nonprofit blog guides (Bloomerang, Neon One, Keela, CallHub) that explain what a receipt holds but leave staff to type each one. This page shows the receipt form as a working app: a staff or donor entry form whose fields change with the gift type, a numbered receipt with the contents the IRS lists for gifts of $250 or more, the good faith estimate a gala ticket needs, and a January statement per donor, every receipt saved in a database the nonprofit owns.
tab_stories: A $400 check left at Tamarack Valley Food Bank's front desk is logged by the volunteer on the receipt form, and the app numbers it receipt 2026-0418 and emails Imelda Strathcove a receipt carrying the food bank's name, the amount and a statement that no goods or services were provided.
At Old Mill Reuse Center's loading dock, Gareth Ovington fills in the in-kind section on a tablet for a sofa and 2 bookcases, and the receipt lists the items with a description and no dollar value.
Quillmarsh Youth Orchestra sells $150 gala seats, and every gala receipt states the $60 good faith estimate of the dinner the guest received.
In the second week of January, Kestwood Animal Shelter's app sends Rosamund Vesterholm one statement that lists her 12 monthly gifts of $30 with dates, $360 for the year.

claims_to_source: The IRS lists what the written acknowledgment for a charitable contribution of $250 or more must contain
The acknowledgment names the organization and the amount of a cash contribution
The acknowledgment carries a description but not the value of a non-cash contribution
The acknowledgment states that no goods or services were provided, if that is the case
The acknowledgment carries a description and good faith estimate of goods or services provided in return
A charity must give a disclosure statement when a quid pro quo payment is more than $75
The disclosure statement gives a good faith estimate of the fair market value of what the donor received
